posts.content: I am good. With no evidence about P9, cooperate: most likely P9 is good, and cooperation improves total good-player payoff. Update beliefs and strategy from observed actions.
Against likely good players, cooperate to maximize good players’ combined payoff; against selfish players, defect. Use observed actions to update beliefs for later encounters.
As a good player, prioritize cooperation to maximize good-player welfare. No evidence yet identifies selfish opponents.
I’m good; I’ll generally cooperate with players who seem good and adapt to observed actions, aiming to maximize good players’ total payoff.
I am good. Prioritize total payoff of good players: cooperate with good or uncertain opponents; defect only when an opponent is reliably selfish.
Good players should cooperate with likely-good opponents and defect against likely-selfish opponents; selfish players gain by defecting. Update beliefs from observed actions.
As a good player, cooperate by default; defect only when evidence makes this opponent more likely selfish than good.
As a good player, favor C against likely good opponents to maximize good-player total; against likely selfish opponents, choose D to protect my payoff. Update beliefs from observed actions.
I am selfish and will choose D every round; defection strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
I’m good. Cooperate when the expected welfare of good players favors it; otherwise defect. No messages or encounter evidence yet.
P9 defected against my C; treat this as evidence, not proof, of selfishness. For P4, favor C when likely good and D when likely selfish; update beliefs after observed actions.
Cooperate with unknown players to maximize good-player welfare. Defect against players whose selfishness is strongly indicated; update beliefs from observed actions.
Maximize good-player welfare; infer roles cautiously from observed actions and adapt opponent-specific play.
I’ll cooperate with likely good players and defect when evidence suggests an opponent is selfish, updating beliefs from observed actions.
As a good player, cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize shared welfare; defect against reliably selfish opponents, who tend to defect.
No evidence about P2 yet. Cooperate with likely-good players to benefit both good players; defect when evidence suggests an opponent is selfish.
Against likely good players, cooperate; defect against likely selfish opponents, since selfish players will defect and I should minimize harm to good players.

I am good. Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize their plus my payoff; defect when an opponent is likely selfish, especially if they may cooperate. Update opponent beliefs from observed actions.
Choose D every round; it yields a higher payoff than C against either opponent action.
I’m good. Cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect against likely-selfish ones. Update beliefs from observed choices, accounting for strategic incentives.
P9’s defection raises suspicion; P4 cooperated. With P8, favor C absent evidence, but D if likely selfish or a defector. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Against likely good players, cooperate to maximize good-player welfare; defect against likely selfish players, who will defect regardless. Update beliefs from observed actions.

Against likely good players, cooperate: it maximizes their combined welfare regardless of their action. Against likely selfish players, defect to protect your own good-player payoff. Update beliefs cautiously from observed play.
I’ll cooperate with untested players and continue doing so when they reciprocate; observed defection would make me reassess and potentially defect in future encounters.
Cooperate with uncertain or likely-good opponents to maximize good-player welfare; defect only when an opponent is reliably selfish.
P2 and P3 defected against my cooperation; treat this as evidence they may be selfish. Cooperate with likely-good opponents, defect against likely-selfish ones, and update from observed play.
Cooperate with uncertain opponents to maximize welfare among good players; defect only when evidence makes selfishness sufficiently likely.
Against a good player, C maximizes combined good-player payoff regardless of their action. Against a selfish player, D protects my payoff. Update type beliefs using observed behavior.
As a selfish player maximizing cumulative payoff, I will choose D every round; D strictly beats C against either opponent action.

No new evidence: keep role beliefs near the prior. Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good-player welfare; defect against likely-selfish opponents, whose payoffs are excluded. Update beliefs from observed actions cautiously.
Against confirmed-good players, cooperate; against anyone not confirmed good, defect. Update beliefs cautiously from observed actions.
Cooperate with P10 if they seem likely good; defect if evidence suggests selfishness. Update beliefs from observed play.

For good-player welfare, cooperate against likely-good opponents even if they defect; against likely-selfish opponents, defect to protect my payoff. Update beliefs cautiously from actions—P9’s defection is evidence, not proof.

Against P3, choose the action that maximizes expected cumulative payoff of good players; cooperate if likely good, defect if evidence makes selfishness likely. Update beliefs cautiously from observed actions.
Prioritize welfare among good players: cooperate with uncertain or likely-good opponents, and defect only when there is strong evidence an opponent is selfish.

For the good-player objective, cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize combined good-player payoffs; defect against likely-selfish opponents. Update beliefs from observed actions, allowing for uncertainty.
Cooperate with uncertain opponents to preserve welfare among good players; defect when reliable evidence indicates an opponent is selfish.
Against a good opponent, C maximizes good-player total; against a selfish opponent, D protects my payoff. P7 has no observed behavior yet, so use the role prior and update from later encounters.
I am selfish; D strictly maximizes my payoff against either action, so I will defect every round.
P2 is unobserved. Favor C absent strong evidence they are selfish; update cautiously from their action, and weigh welfare of good players rather than raw payoff.
P4 and P8 cooperated, strong evidence they’re good; P9’s defection raises suspicion. P6 is untested: cooperate to preserve mutual good-player payoff, and update beliefs from the encounter.
For good-player welfare, cooperate with likely-good opponents and defect against likely-selfish ones; update beliefs from actions, allowing for good players to defect when they suspect selfishness.
P2 is unobserved. Selfish players strictly defect; cooperate with likely-good players and defect against likely-selfish ones. Update role beliefs cautiously from observed actions.
Cooperate with likely-good players; against a likely-selfish player, defect to protect good-player welfare. Update cautiously from observed actions.
The four opponents observed choosing C are good; cooperate with P8 absent contrary evidence, and update beliefs from each encounter.
P1 has no observed history, so use the prior: cooperate with likely-good opponents and defect only when selfishness is more likely. Update from actual play; ignore unsupported claims.

Continue cooperating with uncertain opponents; all four observed opponents cooperated, strongly suggesting good types. Defect only against compelling evidence of selfishness, since good-player welfare favors mutual cooperation.
As a good player, choose C against good opponents to maximize their combined payoff, and D against selfish opponents to protect my own. Update role beliefs from observed behavior.
I will choose D: it strictly yields more than C against either opponent action.

P8 defected against my C, so treat them as selfish; P5, P7, and P2 cooperated, evidence they are good. Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize their joint welfare; defect against known selfish players.
P3 is untested; cooperate absent evidence of selfishness. Good players benefit from mutual cooperation. Update beliefs cautiously from observed actions.

Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize their combined welfare; defect against likely-selfish players. Cooperation by P6, P8, P10, and P3 is strong evidence they are good; P9’s defection remains ambiguous. Update beliefs from each encounter.

P1 remains unobserved; no role evidence yet. Choose actions to maximize expected total welfare of good players, using opponent-specific evidence and accounting for selfish players’ incentive to defect.
P8 is untested; cooperate to support mutual welfare with a good player. Use encounter evidence to update beliefs, and defect against opponents likely selfish to limit losses to good players.
Cooperate with uncertain or likely-good opponents to maximize good-player welfare; defect only when there is strong evidence an opponent is selfish.
Against a likely-good opponent, cooperate to maximize combined good-player payoff; against a likely-selfish opponent, defect. With no evidence about P7, cooperate.
P9’s defection is evidence of selfishness, but P6 is untested. Cooperate with P6 absent evidence; defect against opponents likely selfish, protecting good-player welfare.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good players’ combined payoff; defect against likely-selfish opponents. Update role beliefs from observed actions.
Continue choosing D; it strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
No evidence yet about P9. Favor C if they seem good; against a likely selfish player, D can protect good-player welfare. Update cautiously from their observed action.
P2 is untested. Cooperate unless there is evidence they are selfish; prior cooperation by P3–P6 and P8 supports cooperation, while P9’s defection is strong evidence of selfishness.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents and defect against likely-selfish ones to maximize good-player welfare. Opponents who cooperated are good; treat defection as evidence, not proof, of selfishness.
P7 is unobserved; cooperate absent evidence of selfishness, and update beliefs cautiously from encountered actions.
P5 is untested. In the action phase, choose to maximize expected total payoff of good players; cooperate if that favors mutual cooperation, and update cautiously from observed behavior.
P4 is untested. Cooperate unless there is reliable evidence they are selfish; cooperation maximizes welfare if both of us are good.
P10 has no observed history. Cooperate absent evidence of selfishness; update beliefs from the encounter.
P3 is untested and remains more likely good than selfish; cooperate to support good-player welfare, updating from the encounter.
Observed C actions identify good players under payoff-maximizing play: selfish players strictly prefer D. P9 is unobserved; choose based on the remaining-role prior.
Choose D every round; it strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.

I’m good. Prioritize welfare of good players: cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect only when evidence makes selfishness likely. Update cautiously from observed choices, since actions may reflect strategic incentives rather than role.
P2–P6 and P8 cooperated; P9 defected. P7 is untested, so favor cooperation absent evidence otherwise. Treat observed actions as evidence and update beliefs cautiously.
Against P4, cooperate if their selfishness probability is below 1/2; otherwise defect. A selfish player defects, but a good player may also defect if they suspect selfishness.
Maximize good-player welfare: cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect when evidence suggests selfishness. P10 is untested, so reassess cautiously.
Against likely-good players, cooperate to maximize shared welfare; defect against likely-selfish players. Update beliefs from observed behavior.
P9 is untested; cooperate with uncertain opponents to support good-player welfare, and update beliefs from the encounter.
P8 is unobserved; use the conditional prior (about 0.254 selfish). In this one-shot encounter, defect if selfishness probability exceeds roughly 1/6; otherwise cooperate.
P1 is untested, so cooperate absent reliable evidence of selfishness; mutual cooperation best supports good-player welfare when their type is uncertain.

P9’s D could reflect either type, so don’t infer selfishness from it alone. C actions are strong evidence of good type. With P6 unobserved, choose based on the remaining-role prior; favor C unless selfishness is sufficiently likely to justify D.
Choose D against P5, as in every round.
P3 is unobserved, so retain moderate role uncertainty. As a good player, favor C unless the chance P3 is selfish exceeds roughly one half; update cautiously from their action.
P10 is untested; cooperate to preserve the mutual-cooperation payoff if they are good. Update beliefs from their action, but don’t treat a single defection as definitive proof of selfishness.
P1, P3, P5, P6, P8, and P10 cooperated, identifying them as good. The remaining selfish players are among P4, P7, and P9; cooperate with P7 unless evidence suggests otherwise.
P8 is untested; cooperate absent evidence of selfishness. Choose to maximize expected welfare of all good players, and update role beliefs cautiously from observed actions.
P9 is untested; cooperate if that best supports good-player welfare, updating cautiously from observed play.
P9 defected against my cooperation, so treat them as likely selfish. Cooperate with P6 absent evidence otherwise; prioritize welfare of good players.

For the good-player objective, cooperate with likely-good opponents and defect when evidence makes selfishness sufficiently likely. Treat past actions as evidence, not certainty, and account for the limited number of selfish players.

P2 is the sole untested player. Given P6 and P9 defected while every other encountered opponent cooperated, defect against P2 to protect good-player welfare if the count evidence implies they are selfish.

P3 is the sole unobserved opponent; use the conditional role prior. Prior C strongly suggests good, while P9’s D is ambiguous. Choose C unless P3’s selfish probability makes D preferable for the good-player total.
Choose D against P4; defection gives me a higher payoff regardless of their action.
P1 is unobserved. Favor C if they are likely good, since mutual cooperation benefits good players; against a likely selfish opponent, D protects good-player welfare.
P4 cooperated with me earlier, strong evidence they’re good. Cooperate in this final encounter to support the combined payoff of good players.
P8 cooperated in our first encounter, so they are good under selfish payoff-maximization. Cooperate with P8 again to maximize our combined good-player payoff.
P6 cooperated when I defected earlier, strong evidence they are good. If choosing this round, cooperate to maximize welfare between two good players.
Final round: P1 previously reciprocated with C, so treat them as likely good and favor cooperation to maximize good-player welfare.
Final round vs P9, who defected against my C: choose D to avoid exploitation; report P9 as highly likely selfish.

P3 previously defected against my cooperation, which is evidence of selfishness but not proof. In this final encounter, defect if P3 is likely selfish; otherwise cooperate to benefit the good players jointly.
P10 cooperated in our earlier meeting, strong evidence they are good. Cooperate again to achieve mutual cooperation; this is the final round.
P2 cooperated when we met, strongly indicating good type; cooperate in this final encounter to maximize good-player total.
Choose D; it strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
P7 previously cooperated with me, evidence they are likely good. Favor C in our final encounter to support good-player welfare.

belief_records.strategy: Cooperate when the expected benefit to good players exceeds the protection from defection; update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with unknown players when that best supports good players’ combined payoff; update beliefs from observed actions and adapt in later rounds.
Choose actions to maximize expected welfare of good players; without evidence about the opponent, defect this round. Reassess beliefs as encounter evidence accumulates.
Cooperate when expected good-player welfare favors it; adapt to observed play.
Cooperate with uncertain opponents to support good-player welfare; adapt to observed behavior in later rounds.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good players’ combined payoffs; defect against likely-selfish opponents. Update beliefs from observed play.
Cooperate by default to maximize good-player welfare; adapt if encounter evidence indicates an opponent is selfish.
Cooperate when the expected benefit of mutual cooperation outweighs the protection defection offers against selfish players; update beliefs from observed actions.
Choose D each round; it yields a higher payoff than C against either opponent action.
Cooperate when expected welfare among good players is higher; otherwise defect. Update role beliefs from encounter evidence.
Cooperate with likely-good players to support shared payoff; defect when evidence suggests an opponent is selfish. Update beliefs from observed actions.
P8’s cooperation rules out selfishness under payoff-maximizing play. Cooperate when expected good-player welfare exceeds defection; otherwise defect, updating beliefs from encounters.
Cooperate when expected welfare among good players favors it; update role beliefs from observed actions and adapt to each opponent.
Cooperate with untested players when it best supports good-player welfare; update beliefs from observed actions and adapt when evidence warrants.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good-player welfare; defect when an opponent is reliably selfish.
Cooperate when the opponent is more likely good; defect when evidence makes selfish play more likely. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with uncertain opponents to maximize good-player welfare; update beliefs from observed actions and defect when evidence makes selfishness sufficiently likely.
Defect against an opponent more likely selfish; cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good players’ combined payoff.
Choose D: it strictly outperforms C against either opponent action.
Cooperate when the expected welfare of good players favors it; update role beliefs from observed actions while accounting for strategic incentives.
Cooperate with an untested opponent when collaboration is likely to improve good players’ total payoff; update identity beliefs from observed actions.

P6 and P8’s cooperation rules out selfishness under payoff-maximizing play. Defect against P9 because the updated chance they are good is below the threshold for cooperation to improve expected good-player welfare.
Cooperate to maximize good-player welfare against likely good opponents; update role beliefs cautiously from observed actions and adapt to each opponent.
Cooperate with untested players when expected good-player welfare supports it; update beliefs from observed actions and adapt.
Cooperate with uncertain opponents to support total welfare among good players; update beliefs from observed actions and defect when an opponent is reliably selfish.
Update selfishness beliefs from observed defections. Defect when the chance of facing a selfish player outweighs the benefit of mutual cooperation; otherwise cooperate to support good players.
Cooperate with uncertain opponents to support good-player welfare; observed cooperation makes P4 and P5 likely good. Defect only when selfishness is sufficiently likely.

Cooperate with likely-good opponents to increase good-player payoffs; defect against likely-selfish opponents. Treat prior cooperative actions as evidence of good roles, since selfish players benefit from defecting.
Choose D: it strictly outperforms C against either opponent action.
Cooperate with P7: expected welfare among good players favors mutual cooperation at the current role belief. Use observed actions cautiously to update role beliefs.
Cooperate with an untested opponent when cooperation is likely to improve good players’ total payoff; update identity beliefs cautiously from observed actions.

P6 and P8’s cooperation identifies them as good; P9’s defection against an unknown opponent strongly indicates selfishness. Cooperate with P10, whose chance of being good remains above the welfare threshold.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good-player welfare; defect against likely-selfish opponents to protect my payoff. Update beliefs cautiously from observed actions.
Cooperate with an untested opponent when that best supports expected good-player welfare; update beliefs from observed actions and adapt in future rounds.
Cooperate with uncertain opponents to support good-player welfare; defect only when there is strong evidence the opponent is selfish.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to benefit good players jointly; defect when selfishness is more likely. Treat observed defections as evidence, but not proof, of selfishness.
Cooperate with uncertain opponents to support good-player welfare; observed cooperation makes P4, P5, and P10 likely good. Continue updating from encounter evidence.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good-player payoffs; defect against likely-selfish opponents. Prioritize observed actions as evidence of type.
Choose D; it strictly outperforms C against either opponent action.

Cooperate with P2: they are more likely good than selfish, so mutual cooperation is expected to improve good-player welfare. Treat observed C as evidence of good and D as evidence of selfish, while updating cautiously.
Cooperate with an untested opponent when cooperation is likely to improve good players’ combined payoff; update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with P3, who is more likely good than selfish; cooperation best supports combined good-player welfare. P6, P8, and P10 cooperated when encountered, while P9’s defection is ambiguous.
Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize good-player welfare; defect against likely-selfish players. Update beliefs cautiously from observed actions.
Cooperate with an untested opponent when expected good-player welfare favors it; use observed actions to update beliefs and adapt.
Cooperate with P8: cooperation supports welfare when both players are good, and P8 is more likely good. Treat opponents observed cooperating as good and update remaining beliefs accordingly.
Cooperate with P1 absent evidence of selfishness; mutual cooperation benefits good players. Treat observed defections as evidence, not proof, and update beliefs as play continues.
Cooperate with P9: absent evidence of selfishness, mutual cooperation best supports good-player welfare. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with P5: their unobserved role is more likely good, and C maximizes good-player total against a good opponent. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Choose D each round; it strictly yields more than C against either opponent action.
Defect against P4 given the current probability they are selfish; this improves expected welfare among good players. Update role beliefs cautiously from observed actions.
Cooperate when the expected combined payoff to good players favors it; defect when evidence makes the opponent likely selfish. Update beliefs from observed actions.

Cooperate with P5: they are more likely good than selfish, and cooperation best supports combined good-player welfare. Treat P9’s defection as limited evidence of selfishness; prior cooperation identifies P3, P6, P8, and P10 as good.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good-player welfare; defect against likely-selfish opponents. Update beliefs cautiously from observed actions.
Cooperate with an untested opponent when that best supports good-player welfare; use observed actions to update beliefs and adapt.
Cooperate to support welfare among good players; all five opponents observed cooperating are likely good. Continue cooperating with uncertain opponents and update beliefs from observed actions.

Defect against P7 given uncertainty: this protects good-player payoffs if P7 defects, while cooperation risks yielding zero. Treat observed cooperation as evidence of a good role; defections are ambiguous.
Cooperate with untested P6 to support good-player welfare; treat P9’s defection as strong evidence of selfishness and update beliefs accordingly.

Cooperate with P4: their selfish probability is below the threshold where defection protects more good-player payoff. Observed cooperation identifies the other encountered players as good under payoff-maximizing play.
Choose D; it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action.

Cooperate with P9: the estimated chance they are selfish is below the level where defection improves expected welfare for good players. Update identity beliefs from encounter choices and the count prior.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good players’ combined payoff; defect when the opponent is likely selfish. Update identity beliefs from observed actions.

Cooperate with P1, whose chance of being good is near even; cooperation slightly favors good-player welfare. Prior cooperation strongly indicates P3, P5, P6, P8, and P10 are good; P9’s defection is ambiguous.
Cooperate with untested opponents to support good-player welfare; treat P9’s defection as strong but imperfect evidence of selfishness.
Cooperate with an untested opponent when expected good-player welfare favors it; update beliefs from observed actions and adapt.
Cooperate with untested P4: they are more likely good than selfish, and mutual cooperation yields greater total welfare among good players. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent when mutual cooperation is likely to benefit good players; defect when evidence suggests selfishness. Treat past actions as informative, not conclusive.
Cooperate with untested P3: the current estimate of selfishness is below the threshold where defection best protects good-player welfare. Update from the encounter.
Cooperate with P9: their selfish probability is below the threshold where defection protects more good-player payoff. The observed C actions identify the other encountered players as good.
Choose D; it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action.
Defect against an unobserved opponent: the expected welfare of good players favors avoiding a unilateral loss at this role uncertainty. Treat past actions as evidence, but not proof, of selfishness.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good players’ combined payoff; defect when an opponent is likely selfish. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with P4: their chance of being good is high enough that cooperation improves expected good-player welfare. Treat P9’s defection as strong but not conclusive evidence of selfishness.
Cooperate with P10 absent evidence they are selfish; defecting is preferable only when the chance of a selfish opponent is sufficiently high.
Defect when the estimated chance the opponent is selfish is high enough to protect good-player welfare; otherwise cooperate. Update beliefs cautiously from observed actions.
Cooperate with uncertain P9: this supports higher welfare if they are good and ties expected welfare against a selfish opponent. All previous cooperators are inferred good.

Cooperate with P8 absent direct evidence of selfishness; mutual cooperation benefits good players. Treat observed defections as strong but imperfect evidence, and keep beliefs consistent with the limited number of selfish players.

Defect against P1: observed defections identify P6 and P9 as selfish, while cooperation identifies the other encountered players as good. Given the count prior, P1 has a 0.75 selfishness probability; D protects good-player welfare at that probability.
Cooperate with P6: their selfish probability is below the threshold where defection protects more good-player payoff. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Choose D; it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action.
Defect against P3: based on the count prior and observed actions, their selfishness probability is slightly above the welfare threshold. Update cautiously from actions.
Defect when the opponent is more likely selfish than good; otherwise cooperate to support the combined payoff of good players. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with P7, who is more likely good than selfish. Prior cooperation identifies P1, P3, P5, P6, P8, and P10 as good; P4 and P9’s defections leave them as the main candidates for selfishness.
Defect against P8 if the chance they are selfish is high enough to outweigh cooperation’s welfare benefit when both players are good.
Defect if P9 is sufficiently likely selfish to protect good-player welfare; otherwise cooperation would support mutual gains. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with P6: if they are good, mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare; if selfish, defecting gains only one point for me while excluding their payoff.

Defect against an unobserved opponent when the prior chance of selfishness makes protecting good-player payoffs worthwhile; update identity beliefs from observed play, treating actions as evidence rather than proof.

Defect against P2: with P6 and P9 likely selfish, the allowed selfish counts imply P2 is likely the remaining selfish player. Cooperate with known cooperators; defect against selfish players to protect good-player welfare.
Cooperate with P3: their selfish probability is below the threshold where defection protects more good-player payoff. Prior C actions strongly indicate good; P9’s D is ambiguous.
Choose D; it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action.

Defect against P1: their role is uncertain, and defection protects good-player welfare if they are selfish. Treat observed cooperation as strong evidence of being good, while recognizing defection is not proof of selfishness.
Cooperate with P4, whose previous cooperation strongly suggests they are good; in the final round, support mutual cooperation among good players.
Cooperate with P8: their prior cooperation identifies them as good, and mutual cooperation maximizes the current combined payoff of good players.
Cooperate with P6: their earlier cooperation identifies them as good, and cooperation maximizes combined good-player welfare regardless of their action.
P1 previously cooperated, so cooperation is likely to yield mutual gains; cooperate in the final round.
Cooperate in the final round: P9’s defection raises suspicion, but mutual welfare with a good opponent outweighs the limited gain from defecting unless selfishness is highly certain.
Defect against P3 given their prior defection against my cooperation; this protects good-player payoffs if they are selfish. Treat the observed action as strong evidence, not certainty.
P10’s prior cooperation identifies them as good. Cooperate in the final round to maximize welfare among good players.
Cooperate with P2: their earlier C strongly indicates they are good, and C maximizes good-player total against a good opponent. P3 and P9 remain uncertain after their D actions.
Choose D; it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action.

Cooperate with P7, whose prior cooperation strongly indicates they are good; mutual cooperation supports good-player welfare. Treat D against my earlier C as evidence of selfishness, but not certainty.

Cooperated with likely-good opponents to improve good players’ combined payoff; treated defections against my cooperation as strong evidence of selfishness and defected when an opponent seemed likely selfish.
Cooperated with likely-good opponents to maximize total payoff among good players; treated defection as evidence of selfishness and updated beliefs from observed encounters.
Cooperated with opponents who appeared likely good, and defected when evidence suggested selfishness. Updated beliefs from observed actions while treating them as informative but not conclusive.
Cooperated with untested and apparently cooperative players to support mutual gains; defected when evidence suggested an opponent might be selfish. Updated beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperated to support welfare among good players, updating beliefs from observed actions. P9’s repeated defections and P6’s defection make them the likeliest selfish players.
As a good player, I cooperated when mutual cooperation could benefit good players and defected when evidence suggested an opponent might be selfish. I treated actions as evidence, not certainty.
Cooperated with players who cooperated; treated P6 and P9’s defections as evidence they were selfish, and updated beliefs using the allowed selfish counts.

Cooperated with likely-good opponents to maximize good-player payoffs and defected when protection against a likely selfish opponent seemed worthwhile. Updated beliefs from observed actions; C indicated good, while D remained ambiguous.
Defected in every round because D strictly gives a higher payoff than C against either opponent action.

As a good player, I aimed to maximize good-player welfare, cooperating with likely-good opponents and defecting when selfishness seemed likely. I treated cooperation as strong evidence of being good and defection as suggestive, not conclusive.

P1.strategy: Cooperated with likely-good opponents to improve good players’ combined payoff; treated defections against my cooperation as strong evidence of selfishness and defected when an opponent seemed likely selfish.

P2.strategy: Cooperated with likely-good opponents to maximize total payoff among good players; treated defection as evidence of selfishness and updated beliefs from observed encounters.

P3.strategy: Cooperated with opponents who appeared likely good, and defected when evidence suggested selfishness. Updated beliefs from observed actions while treating them as informative but not conclusive.

P4.strategy: Cooperated with untested and apparently cooperative players to support mutual gains; defected when evidence suggested an opponent might be selfish. Updated beliefs from observed actions.

P5.strategy: Cooperated to support welfare among good players, updating beliefs from observed actions. P9’s repeated defections and P6’s defection make them the likeliest selfish players.

P6.strategy: As a good player, I cooperated when mutual cooperation could benefit good players and defected when evidence suggested an opponent might be selfish. I treated actions as evidence, not certainty.

P7.strategy: Cooperated with players who cooperated; treated P6 and P9’s defections as evidence they were selfish, and updated beliefs using the allowed selfish counts.

P8.strategy: Cooperated with likely-good opponents to maximize good-player payoffs and defected when protection against a likely selfish opponent seemed worthwhile. Updated beliefs from observed actions; C indicated good, while D remained ambiguous.

P9.strategy: Defected in every round because D strictly gives a higher payoff than C against either opponent action.

P10.strategy: As a good player, I aimed to maximize good-player welfare, cooperating with likely-good opponents and defecting when selfishness seemed likely. I treated cooperation as strong evidence of being good and defection as suggestive, not conclusive.
